bc_red_tail_group.blurb: Red Tail Group is a cluster of crags within Skaha Bluffs, in the Okanagan near Penticton. It is mostly sport, with a large share of trad. Across Skaha the cliffs are mainly coarse gneiss, and these crags face the sun for most of the day, though the lower walls are partly shaded by trees. Grades centre on 5.10, with a solid run of 5.6 to 5.9 below it and some 5.11 above. Lower Red Tail holds the most climbs, followed by Another Buttress, Red Tail South and Upper Red Tail.

ca_eastern_hills.blurb: Eastern Hills is a remote collection of sport and trad crags east of Mammoth Lakes, in the Eastern Sierra. Trad outnumbers sport here, and there are a couple of top-rope lines. Grades mostly fall between 5.8 and 5.10, with 5.10 the largest group and very little harder. Benton Crags holds the most climbs, followed by the Sagehen Summit Area. At Benton Crags the rock is grainy granite, the routes are mostly easy and moderate, and the walls mainly face west and south.

ct_westwoods_cockaponset_state_forest.blurb: Westwoods is bouldering only, spread across Guilford and Branford from the edge of I-95 to the coastal marshes. The setting is lowland forest near the shore, scattered with granite ledges, outcrops and boulders left behind by retreating glaciers. The grades skew easy to moderate, with most problems between V0 and V5 and a thinner tail of hard ones up to V12. The Bunny Boulder Area holds the most climbs, followed by the Granite Road area, Roadside Boulder In The Cut and The Rock Canopy. At the Bunny Boulder Area the problems run from V2 to V10.

va_mill_creek.blurb: Mill Creek is bouldering only, west of Blacksburg. The rock is sandstone: boulders near the creek are grainy, while those higher on the hillsides are tighter-grained, with slopers, edges, pockets and pinches. The grades are friendly, with most problems between V1 and V4 and a smaller set of harder ones up to V9. The Beach holds the most climbs, followed by Butternut Hill, the Waterfall Area and Genesis. At the Beach, problems from V0 to V9 are spread over five boulder groups.

wv_bridge_area.blurb: The Bridge Area is a group of crags in the New River Gorge proper, around the New River Gorge Bridge. Most climbing is trad, with a smaller amount of sport and a set of boulders. All of the crags face south. Gorge climbing in general is on sandstone along the rims, and the rock is highly featured, with jugs, pockets, huecos and slopers. Grades are mostly 5.9 to 5.12, with 5.10 and 5.11 the largest groups. Bridge Buttress holds the most climbs, followed by Promised Area, the Bridge Boulders, Maranatha Area and First Strike Area.

_skipped.pa_susquehanna_riverlands_state_park: Mountain Project's pages for its areas say climbing is not yet permitted at the park, so it is closed to climbing; no two usable pages.
